title: Taslima Nasrin at Litmus'25: The Speech You Must Not Skip
description:
Taslima Nasrin’s full, uncut Litmus ’25 speech with subtitles. A powerful call for atheism, rationalism, free speech, women’s rights, and secularism—delivered to a packed stadium in Kochi, Kerala. In this talk, Taslima explains why criticism of religion isn’t hate, how secular education and separation of religion and state protect human rights, and why freedom of expression includes the right to offend. 

If you’ve searched for Taslima Nasrin speech, Litmus 25, atheism in India, secularism, women’s rights, free speech, rationalism, esSENSE Global, this video gives you the rational perspective. Don’t forget to subscribe, like, comment, and share to support evidence-based voices.

Many intellectuals who themselves enjoy the benefits of secularism in their own countries refuse to criticize the Islamic oppression of women, fearing that it might hurt the religious sentiments of Muslims. Never be possible to end Islam based politics. And if that doesn't happen, Islamic states will remain in darkness forever. Women will never enjoy the right to live as full human beings. As a child, I was forced to read verses from the Quran, but I could not understand the meaning of the words I recited. Like other children, I was merely paring sounds. Our language was Bengali, not Arabic. No matter how many times I repeated and memorized the verses, I had no way of knowing what I was saying. I was told that Allah wanted the Quran to be read in its original language. But that only made me more curious to know its meaning. One day I discovered a Bengali translation of the Quran. I read it every word of that so-called holy book. And guess what? I became an atheist. >> [applause] >> I did not need to read any book on atheism, secularism or humanism to become an atheist. I still believe that for Muslims, the Quran itself is the best book to inspire atheism. >> [applause] >> As I grew up, I realized that like other religions, Islam is not compatible with human rights, women's rights, freedom of expression or democracy. In a true democracy, separation of religion and state is absolutely essential. There can be no women's rights under religious law. There can be no human rights in a society governed by religious rules. Freedom of speech and expression must include the right to differ, to offend as well as to praise, a truth that most people in many countries neither know nor accept. Without the right to offend, freedom of expression cannot exist. And without freedom of expression, democracy will not work. Islam does not regard women as independent human beings. A woman does not have the right to charge her husband in a similar manner. Women are not allowed to inherit property on equal terms with their brothers. In case in the case of inheritance, Allah says that a male shall inherit twice as much as a female. And after all the rights and freedoms, after obtaining all the sexual pleasures and the pleasure of being the master, Allah will reward men with wine, food, and 72 virgins in paradise, including the wives they had on earth. And what is the reward for the pious woman? Nothing. nothing but the same old husband, the same man who caused her suffering while they were on earth. It was easy for me to become an atheist. I was a student of science. So, it was hard to accept that the sun moves around the earth, that the moon has its own light or that the purpose of mountains is to support the earth. So it will not fall down somewhere. I came to suspect and later to be sure that the Quran was not written by someone who had any knowledge of science. Not only did I read the Quran, I also read the hadith, the words of Muhammad. I found many events in the prophet Muhammad's life in which whenever he faced a problem, Allah conveniently solved it for him. For example, when he was sexually aroused after seeing his daughter-in-law, Allah sent him a message saying that he could marry her because his son was adopted and therefore not his real son. So the marriage was was justified. Further, he created a new rule. Muslims would no longer be allowed to adopt children. Muhammad married 11 times, one of his brides being six-year-old Aayisha. He said Allah told him that he was allowed to enjoy his wives, his female slaves, and all the captive women he possessed. Even though widow marriage was legal at the time, he made it illegal for men to marry any of his wives after his death. It became clear to me that Muhammad had written the Quran for his own interest, for his own comfort, and for his own pleasure. When I studied other religions, I found that they too oppressed women. I'm sure you have often heard that Islam does not support the killing of innocent people, that Allah of the Holy Quran never advocates killing and that such acts are the work of a few misguided individuals at the fringes of society. We are told that Islam means peace, that Islam means tolerance. But is this true? Does Islam really preach peace, tolerance, and nonviolence? Those Muslims who perpetrate crimes in the name of Allah think otherwise. They believe that they do they believe what they do is jihad or holy war. They believe that killing non-believers is mandatory for every Muslim. Those who blow up their own bodies to kill people of different faiths do so because they believe they will be rewarded in paradise. They hope to be blessed by Allah to eat celestial food, drink pure wine, and enjoy the company of virgins. When the prophet was in Mecca I think and still not powerful he called for tolerance saying to you be your religion and to be to and to me mine. The famous quote is often mis misused to prove that the general principle of the Quran is one of tolerance. He advised his followers to speak kindly to their enemies. exhorted them to be patient and said there is no compulsion in religion. But all that changed drastically when he came to power. Then killing and slaying non-believers was justified in countless verses with harshness and without mercy. The verses quoted to prove Islam's tolerance ignore the many others that bear no trace of tolerance or forgiveness. The prophet himself set an example of violence by invading Jewish settlement, breaking treaties he had signed with them and banishing some after confiscating their belongings, massacring others and taking their wives and children as slaves. to his soldiers. He distributed the women captured in his raids, keeping the prettiest for himself. These are not stories but records from authentic Islamic history and the hadith. One can argue that such behavior was not unknown or unusual among conquerors and leaders of the medieval world. But it is certainly not befitting of a peaceful saint or of someone who claimed to be the mercy for all creation. I have been fighting every day against injustice and inequality, against religious terrorism and superstition, against bigotry and obscurantism. I have been fighting for human rights, women's rights, freedom of expression, and humanism. I do not fear to tell the truth. My crime was, I said, religious scriptures are out of time and out of place. You know, I have no home. I'm a Bengali writer, but I have no place in Bengal. Bangladesh expelled me. Even West Bengal threw me out of the country for no fault of mine. But I have a home. My home is the heart. The heart of every rationalist, the heart of every freethinker, the heart of every secularist, the heart of every humanist. Their solidarity is my shelter. Their love is my country. >> [applause] >> I regret nothing. I will not retreat until my last breath. I will fight against fundamentalism, against extremism, against intolerance. I will fight for freedom, for equality, for human dignity. I, for one, will not be silenced. I will not be silenced. Come what may. Thank you. Thank you very much. [applause] [music]
